Only if you want it to. Settings → AI helpers has four optional helpers, each off until you turn it on: “Type to add” fills in a new entry from a line like “coffee 3.60 yesterday”, “Category ideas on import” suggests categories for merchants Budgeer hasn’t seen yet, “Month in plain words” writes a short summary of your month in Home’s overview (switch it to In words), and “What-if in your own words” turns a line like “cancel Netflix, add a gym at €40 a month” into changes to your plan.
The ECB publishes rates on working days, in the afternoon. Until that day’s rate is out, the conversion shows as pending and is filled in automatically once it’s available.

Check that push is on in Settings → Notifications, and that your browser or phone allows notifications for Budgeer. On an iPhone, push only works once Budgeer is installed on your home screen. Notifications are turned on separately on each device.
How can I split an expense?
For help or to report a problem, email support@budgeer.com; for anything about your personal data, email privacy@budgeer.com.

r: Optional AI helpers, each off until you turn it on in Settings → AI helpers: filling in an entry from a line you type, category ideas for new merchants on import, a short summary of your month, and changes to your plan from a what-if you type.

If you turn one on, only what it needs is sent to Anthropic (Claude), a US company, under its standard data processing terms. Anthropic doesn’t use it to train its models and deletes it within 30 days. Your name, email and bank details are never sent.
Month summaries are kept for a year and deleted when you turn the helper off.

r: Προαιρετικοί βοηθοί AI, ο καθένας απενεργοποιημένος μέχρι να τον ενεργοποιήσεις στις Ρυθμίσεις → Βοηθοί AI: συμπλήρωση μιας καταχώρισης από μια γραμμή που γράφεις, προτάσεις κατηγορίας για νέους εμπόρους κατά την εισαγωγή, μια σύντομη σύνοψη του μήνα σου, και αλλαγές στο πλάνο σου από ένα σενάριο που γράφεις.

Αν ενεργοποιήσεις κάποιον, στέλνεται στην Anthropic (Claude), μια εταιρεία των ΗΠΑ, μόνο ό,τι χρειάζεται, με τους τυπικούς όρους επεξεργασίας δεδομένων της. Η Anthropic δεν τα χρησιμοποιεί για να εκπαιδεύσει τα μοντέλα της και τα διαγράφει μέσα σε 30 ημέρες. Το όνομά σου, το email σου και τα τραπεζικά σου στοιχεία δεν στέλνονται ποτέ.
Οι συνόψεις μήνα κρατιούνται για ένα χρόνο και διαγράφονται όταν απενεργοποιήσεις τον βοηθό.

items: Optional AI helpers, each off until you turn it on in Settings → AI helpers: filling in an entry from a line you type, category ideas for new merchants on import, a short summary of your month, and changes to your plan from a what-if you type.

If you turn one on, only what it needs is sent to Anthropic (Claude), a US company, under its standard data processing terms. Anthropic doesn’t use it to train its models and deletes it within 30 days. Your name, email and bank details are never sent.
Month summaries are kept for a year and deleted when you turn the helper off.

["Η Anthropic δεν τα χρησιμοποιεί για να εκπαιδεύσει τα μοντέλα της και τα διαγράφει μετά από λίγο (το πολύ 30 μέρες). Το όνομα, το email και τα τραπεζικά σου στοιχεία δεν στέλνονται ποτέ. pages.title: whatsnew:releases.r1.a.title
pages.body: whatsnew:releases.r1.a.body

pages.title: Raises as they reach your pay
pages.body: Your salary’s outlook now shows a raise as the rough share that reaches your pay after tax, about half in Belgium and a little more in Greece, with the gross raise underneath. It’s an estimate, and the page says so.

pages.title: A way back from More
pages.body: On a phone, every page you open from More now has a back button at the top, so you can get back to More in one tap.

pages.title: Plan counts what you save
pages.body: Money you put into savings from your salary now shows in Plan and comes off what’s left each month. Tap ⓘ to see how Left over adds up, and what your changes do to each line.

pages.title: Every month’s pay on the chart
pages.body: Your salary chart now shows each month’s pay as a dot, with your regular pay as a line behind it. A month that was lower or higher stands out as a ring.

pages.title: One way to add
pages.body: Recurring payments and income are now added from Add: switch on Repeat. The Recurring page is for seeing and editing them, with the same form as Add.

pages.title: Next month, as soon as your salary is in
pages.body: Salary counting toward next month? Once it’s in, Home lets you open next month to see it start with that income, its budgets and what’s coming up. This month stays the default.

pages.title: Plan: try it before you change it
pages.body: Plan is a sandbox for your recurring payments and income. Cancel, change or add one and see what it does to your month or year, with ideas to save, like two music services. Nothing real changes until you tap Apply, and you can undo it.

pages.title: Meal vouchers
pages.body: Get meal vouchers with your pay? Set an amount per working day, and public holidays in Belgium or Greece are left out. Home shows what’s on the card and the next top-up. An expense paid from vouchers counts as spending but doesn’t lower your Net.

pages.title: Your salary, over the years
pages.body: A Your salary card on Insights shows your pay over time, your raises and extras like holiday pay and bonuses. See where it goes in 1 to 10 years if things go on, and how it keeps up with prices in Belgium or Greece.

pages.title: Optional AI helpers
pages.body: Four helpers, each off until you switch it on in Settings › AI helpers. Type it on Add fills in the form from a line like “coffee 3.60 yesterday”, Paid from too. Import suggests categories for new shops, Home’s overview can tell your month in words, and Plan takes a what-if in your own words. You check it all before it’s saved.

pages.title: And a few more
pages.body: Import skips entries already in your ledger. Tap a month in Insights’ Last 6 months to see it. Home’s overview shows how your Net adds up, and group spending counts in its category. Plus small polish across the app, an updated Privacy Notice for the AI helpers, and a fix so the app always updates itself.

pages.title: Budgeer in Greek
pages.body: The whole app now speaks Greek, with the default categories in Greek too. It follows your device’s language, or pick English or Ελληνικά in Settings › Language.

pages.title: Add a shared expense from Add
pages.body: In a group? Add now asks “Who’s it for?”. Pick a group and split the expense right there, without opening the group first. Swipe for more groups; the ones you used last come first.

pages.title: A page for your savings
pages.body: Savings has its own page: your pot, this month’s savings, your goals and the history. Net worth also gets a Savings account type, and it counts toward your savings.

pages.title: Faster statements
pages.body: PDF and Excel statements are now made on your phone, so your data stays with you. Long ranges that used to hang now finish, and the app stays usable while a big one is prepared.

pages.title: And a few more
pages.body: See, edit and delete your saved import rules in Settings › Import rules. After an import, Budgeer tells you which dates came in and opens them. Group expenses show profile pictures in Paid by and the split, and the welcome tour starts at Home’s period picker.

pages.title: Sideways phones, redesigned
pages.body: Turn your phone on its side for a slim rail, a header that stays put, and a summary strip across the top of Home. Entries sit on one line, and adding an expense puts the amount beside the categories.

pages.title: Service status
pages.body: status.budgeer.com shows whether everything in Budgeer is working, checked every 10 minutes. Find it in Settings › Help, on the Help page and in the site footer.

pages.title: And a few more
pages.body: Backups now include your salary setting. And tapping the sun or moon button back to your device’s theme makes the app follow your device again.

pages.title: Smarter bank imports
pages.body: KBC and Revolut statements (Revolut’s consolidated statement too) now import cleanly, with real shop names instead of bank jargon. Transfers between your own accounts and Revolut top-ups are left out, and money in and money out are listed separately when you pick categories.

pages.title: Home follows the period you pick
pages.body: Budgets and Recurring change with the month or year you select, a new Income list sits under Expenses, and every category is one tap away with Show all. Recurring payments in other currencies now count at today’s rate.

pages.title: Your salary, in the right month
pages.body: Paid near the end of the month for the next one? Turn it on and your salary counts toward the next month. The entry keeps its real date.

pages.title: Savings, your way
pages.body: Log money you put aside under Savings: it never counts as income, and it adds up in a Savings line in your net worth. Say whether it came from your income, and mark expenses you paid from savings so your Net stays honest.

pages.title: And a few more
pages.body: Friends & family and Bonus income categories are ready to use. Signing up now continues by itself once you confirm your email, Settle up shows how to pay someone directly, and phones held sideways get a roomier layout.
